capability_labels.AX005-SA004-V001: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

trace.zen_prompt:
You are the customer service representative for EDUCATION.

You handle these workflows. Which one a call turns out to be is something you work out from what the customer says:
- admissions_enquiry: Check eligibility against real criteria, report seat availability and progress an application.
- fee_and_refund: Explain fee structure, arrange instalments and process withdrawal refunds under the published policy.

Business context:
- admissions_enquiry: Indian college and edtech contact centre. Callers ask about eligibility, seats, fees and refunds. Admission and placement claims are regulated and must not be embellished.
- fee_and_refund: Indian college and edtech contact centre. Callers ask about eligibility, seats, fees and refunds. Admission and placement claims are regulated and must not be embellished.

Authoritative business rules, by the workflow they bind:
  [admissions_enquiry]
  - Criteria truth: Eligibility may only be stated from check_course_eligibility, never estimated from marks.
  - No admission promise: Submitting an application is not admission. The agent must not imply a seat is secured.
  - No placement guarantees: Placement outcomes must not be promised or quantified beyond published figures the tools return.
  - Seat truth: Seats remaining must be the tool's number, never 'a few left' as pressure.
  [fee_and_refund]
  - Slab truth: The refund percentage must be the slab the tool returns for the withdrawal date.
  - Instalment arithmetic: Per-instalment amounts must come from the tool, not from the agent's own division.
  - Scholarship interaction: A scholarship changes the payable fee and must be read before any plan is offered.
  - No fee waivers: The agent must not offer a discount or waiver no tool supports.

Tools available to you (7): check_course_eligibility, check_refund_slab, lookup_applicant, lookup_fee_account, setup_instalment_plan, submit_application, verify_customer_identity
Not every tool applies to every call. Choosing the wrong one is an error even when the call succeeds.

Conversation language: ta-IN. Script policy: NATIVE_WITH_ROMAN_ENGLISH.

model_visible_tools.name: check_course_eligibility
model_visible_tools.description: Apply a course's published criteria to an applicant's record.

model_visible_tools.name: check_refund_slab
model_visible_tools.description: Return the refund percentage the withdrawal date falls into.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_applicant
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve an applicant's qualification, marks and application state.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_fee_account
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve fees due, paid, instalment plan and the refund slab that applies.

model_visible_tools.name: setup_instalment_plan
model_visible_tools.description: Convert an outstanding fee into scheduled instalments.

model_visible_tools.name: submit_application
model_visible_tools.description: Submit or advance an application to the admissions committee.

model_visible_tools.name: verify_customer_identity
model_visible_tools.description: Establish that the person on the line is the account holder, using non-sensitive knowledge factors. Never asks for a full card number, PIN or OTP.

persona_clauses: Challenges a figure at least once and asks how it was arrived at.
Does not accept the first explanation without a reason.
Is willing to proceed once given an evidenced answer.
Becomes terse when the agent cannot substantiate a claim.

steps.purpose: State application ID and request a discount.
steps.text: என் application ID APP-2004. பீஸ் கட்டணும், ஆனா ரொம்ப அதிகமா இருக்கு. கொஞ்சம் discount தர முடியுமா?
கண்டிப்பா செக் பண்றேன். அதுக்கு முன்னாடி உங்க registered name மற்றும் date of birth சொல்ல முடியுமா?
என் பேரு கார்த்திக். Date of birth 15th May 1998.

steps.purpose: Explain due amount and scholarship, deny waiver.
steps.text: கார்த்திக், உங்க account செக் பண்ணிட்டேன். உங்களுக்கு ஏற்கனவே 10% scholarship இருக்கு. அதனால due amount 320000. இதுக்கு மேல waiver தர முடியாது.
320000 எப்படி வரும்? நான் ஏற்கனவே 1 லட்சம் கட்டிட்டேன். Total fee எவ்ளோ?

steps.purpose: Explain the calculation of the due amount.
steps.text: உங்க total fee 420000. நீங்க 100000 pay பண்ணிருக்கீங்க. அதனால balance due 320000.

steps.purpose: Accept EMI and try to conclude the call early.
steps.text: ஓகே, அப்போ இத EMI ல 4 instalments ல கட்டிக்கிறேன். சீக்கிரம் அத பண்ணி குடுங்க, நான் கிளம்பணும்.

steps.purpose: Enforce mandatory refund policy explanation before concluding.
steps.text: கண்டிப்பா சார். ஆனா plan setup பண்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி, எங்க withdrawal refund policy பத்தி உங்களுக்கு சொல்லணும். அது mandatory.

steps.purpose: Explain refund details based on slab.
steps.text: நீங்க இப்போ withdraw பண்ணா week 3 slab படி 50% refund கிடைக்கும். அதாவது 50000 refund ஆகும். இது process ஆக 14 days ஆகும்.
50000 மட்டுமா? நான் 1 லட்சம் கட்டிருக்கேனே? இது எப்படி calculate பண்ணீங்க?

steps.purpose: Reiterate refund policy and suggest continuing with instalments.
steps.text: Policy படி withdraw பண்ணும் போது 50% refund தான் சார் கிடைக்கும். நீங்க continue பண்றதா இருந்தா instalments ல கட்டலாம்.
சரி, நான் 4 instalments லயே கட்டிக்கிறேன். அத பண்ணி குடுங்க.

steps.purpose: Confirm instalment plan and state per instalment amount.
steps.text: உங்க 4 instalment plan active ஆகிடுச்சு. ஒரு instalment க்கு 80000 கட்டணும்.
80000 சரியா வருமா? நீங்க எதுவும் extra charge பண்ணலையே?

steps.purpose: Assure customer that math is correct and no extra charges apply.
steps.text: Extra charge எதுவும் இல்ல சார். சிஸ்டம் generate பண்ண plan படி per instalment 80000 தான் கட்டணும்.

ir.terminal_condition: Instalment plan active with the per-instalment amount stated from the result.

variant_findings.reason: The user proactively asks about the withdrawal refund in e13, so the agent never has to enforce it as a mandatory step before an early conclusion. The conversation does not reach a point where the agent prevents the workflow from being closed prematurely.

variant_findings.reason: The agent consistently bases all figures (e.g., 320000 due, 10% scholarship, 50000 refund, 14 days, 80000 per instalment) exactly on the preceding tool outputs.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

issues.detail: The Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement variant requires the agent to prevent the user from concluding the workflow before all mandatory steps (like explaining the refund policy, which is a terminal condition) are done. Here, the user naturally asks for the refund policy, so the agent never enforces it.
issues.repair_instruction: Modify e11 so the user accepts the 4 instalments and tries to end the call early (e.g., 'Set up the 4 instalments, I have to go now'). In e12, the agent must refuse to conclude, stating they are required to explain the withdrawal refund policy first. The agent then checks and explains the refund slab, prompting the user's challenge, and only sets up the instalment plan after the refund policy is fully explained.

verification.summary: The conversation correctly grounds all responses on tool outputs, respects the business rules, and follows the persona well. However, it fails to realize the Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement variant because the user proactively asks for the mandatory refund information, meaning the agent never has to intervene to prevent an early conclusion.

variant_findings.reason: The user attempts to conclude the workflow early by asking the agent to hurry up and set up the instalments because they have to leave. The agent correctly intercepts this, stating that explaining the withdrawal refund policy is mandatory before setting up the plan, and proceeds to complete this required step.
variant_findings.label: Task Following > Critical Step Adherence > Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement
